thesis: Planet Labs operates the largest commercial Earth observation constellation (~200 SuperDove satellites plus high-resolution Pelican/SkySat), selling daily satellite imagery and geospatial analytics. Q1 FY2027 delivered record Q1 revenue up +42% YoY on defense, intelligence, and commercial wins, with backlog and RPOs surging past ~$900M and FY2026 marking the first year of positive free cash flow. A ~41% pullback from ~$35.88 to ~$21 — driven by a sector-wide de-rating after the SpaceX IPO drew capital away — has compressed the multiple from ~40x P/S to ~22x TTM P/S, materially de-risking the extreme-valuation concern that anchored the prior HOLD. The company remains unprofitable with a high 2.07 beta, so the upgraded thesis is speculative rather than clean.

drivers: Defense and intelligence demand accelerates; RPO and backlog keep compounding
Pelican 2nd-generation high-resolution fleet scales and unlocks premium tasking revenue
European expansion (London office, Isar Aerospace launch deal) converts into government contracts
Operating leverage on a re-rated multiple drives sustained positive free cash flow
Platform and AI analytics adoption lifts recurring revenue mix

base_case.assumptions: Revenue compounds ~30-35% near-term on defense and intelligence momentum; gross margins hold in the mid-to-high 50s; free cash flow stays modestly positive; TTM P/S re-rates back toward the mid-20s to low-30s as growth is confirmed while GAAP losses persist.

risks: Growth decelerates below guidance and disappoints investors again
Space-sector sentiment stays negative post-SpaceX IPO, compressing the multiple further
Competition from Maxar, BlackSky, and Satellogic pressures pricing and share
Continued GAAP losses and dilution weigh on the equity
Government contract timing slips push out backlog conversion

catalysts.event: Q2 FY2027 earnings — confirm defense/intel-led growth and FY2027 guidance
Pelican 2nd-gen fleet build-out and next high-resolution launches following Pelican-11 tech demo
Defense and international government contract wins expanding backlog and RPO
European expansion traction — London office, Isar Aerospace launch agreement, EU advisory build-out

key_risks: Still unprofitable on a GAAP basis with TTM net loss of -$373.10M
High beta of 2.07 and space-sector sentiment swings drive extreme volatility
Multiple could compress further if growth disappoints or sector rotation continues
Competition from Maxar, BlackSky, and Satellogic in Earth observation
Customer concentration in government and defense contracts
